key_themes: Nvidia RTX Spark AI PC chip launch reshapes competitive landscape, lifting tech stocks while pressuring Intel and Qualcomm
Dual mega-deal day: Berkshire Hathaway acquires Taylor Morrison for $8.5B and Barry Diller bids $18B for MGM Resorts
US-Iran military escalation reignites oil supply fears, crude surges 3% to $90+ despite record stock highs

stocks.reason: Shares surged 6%+ after CEO Jensen Huang unveiled RTX Spark, a new AI-focused processor for personal computers, calling it "as big a deal as the reinvention of the phone into a smartphone"
Stock jumped 27% intraday and surged ~37% after hours after Q2 earnings crushed estimates — the biggest beat since 2018 — and raised full-year guidance; trading volume was 287% above average
Shares popped 22% after Berkshire Hathaway announced an $8.5 billion enterprise-value cash acquisition at $72.50/share (24% premium), the first major deal under new CEO Greg Abel
Stock jumped 8-13% after Barclays initiated coverage at Overweight with a $350 price target, calling IBM's quantum computing strategy a "Nvidia-like" playbook; Barclays bull case is $449
Shares rose 10.7% as AI infrastructure demand accelerated alongside Nvidia's RTX Spark announcement, with Dell seen as a key AI PC ecosystem beneficiary
Barry Diller's People Inc. (formerly IAC) submitted a non-binding proposal to buy all remaining MGM shares for $48.30/share in cash, valuing MGM at ~$18 billion including debt
Shares surged 12% after company disclosed its data center solutions unit generated $302.7M in 2025 revenue and projected 65% growth in 2026, signaling AI infrastructure demand
Stock rose 7-8% and saw highly unusual call options activity (bullish skew) after announcing a new AI-compatible PC product line in partnership with Nvidia's RTX Spark processor
Shares tumbled 7% as Nvidia's RTX Spark AI PC chip announcement raised competitive concerns, threatening Qualcomm's Snapdragon X dominance in AI PC processors
Stock fell 6%+ as Nvidia's new RTX Spark PC processor directly threatens Intel's historically dominant PC chip market position
Shares plunged as much as 12% after the company filed an 8-K disclosing "substantial doubt about the Company's ability to continue as a going concern," citing declining sales and rising memory costs
Filed a mixed shelf registration seeking to raise $80 billion in fresh capital, with proceeds earmarked for accelerated AI expansion including data centers and AI infrastructure
Shares gained ~9.71% amid a broad AI software rally sparked by Nvidia's RTX Spark announcement, as investors rotated into enterprise software names expected to benefit from AI-enabled PC adoption
Shares rose alongside enterprise software peers (Asana, Adobe) as Nvidia's RTX Spark AI PC chip announcement sparked optimism for software companies that serve AI-enabled enterprise workflows
